title: Restore Drill
summary: Prove a Postgres backup restores in an isolated Docker network.
user: A small team self-hosting Postgres and application data that needs recurring proof that a backup can restore into a usable isolated environment, not merely that a job completed.
smallest_useful_product: A Docker-first CLI that restores a chosen Postgres dump/volume into an isolated network, runs configurable SQL/HTTP smoke assertions, records duration and artifact hashes, then tears it down.
success_measure: A weekly drill succeeds unattended for four weeks and reports a measured recovery time; an intentionally broken backup is detected before the next scheduled drill.
constraints: Never target production endpoints; require an explicit disposable Docker network; protect dumps with local paths/credential files and securely delete temporary volumes where practical.
